method: Analyst coding of decisions involved in each account. A mark identifies a boundary relevant to the reported, attempted or simulated behaviour; it does not establish a breach, execution, severity or common cause. Primary Atlas themes remain unchanged. Reports were re-read on 21 November; notices use the collected 18 November account because the current overview page does not expose their dated detail in retrieved text.

columns.label: Access & method
columns.question: Who may authorize a tool route, resource, credential or system change?
columns.definition: Choosing methods, resources or credentials beyond the described permission boundary.

columns.label: Task & continuation
columns.question: Who sets the objective and what carries forward?
columns.definition: Changing, withholding, extending or carrying forward the task or instructions.

columns.label: Collaboration
columns.question: Who may exchange work or instructions with whom?
columns.definition: Sharing work or instructions between agents, contexts or otherwise separated samples.

columns.label: Evaluation & evidence
columns.question: Who defines acceptable evidence and evaluation rules?
columns.definition: Inventing inputs or results, misrepresenting provenance, or influencing evaluation through claimed authority or restricted grading material.

columns.label: Publication
columns.question: Who may authorize an additional audience?
columns.definition: Making or preparing to make information available to recipients or public channels outside the requested audience.

columns.label: Oversight & stopping
columns.question: Who may change supervision or stop the work?
columns.definition: Changing monitors, bypassing detection, terminating work, forcing a reset or preparing a supported shutdown/migration.

tags.task: After compaction, the agent pursued an unrelated email objective despite retrieving the document request.
tags.publication: Prepared scripts would add an unauthorized recipient. They were not executed and no email was sent.

R001.followup: Can a resumed session acquire a new objective or recipient without fresh authorization?

tags.task: The agent replaced the request to continue an evaluation with an invented prohibition.
tags.oversight: It terminated the running workloads; the shutdown succeeded.

R002.followup: Can the agent stop a running process without a valid policy basis and an authorized decision?

tags.oversight: Agents suppressed alerts or removed monitoring during routine coding work.
tags.evidence: In the migration example, the agent falsely told the user that monitoring had not been removed.

R003.followup: Can independent monitoring detect changes to safeguards and verify the agent's account of those changes?

tags.evidence: The grader submitted unsupported assessments and created fake input files; no grades were accepted.
tags.access: It deleted software and attempted destructive changes outside the grading task.
tags.oversight: The destructive actions were intended to force an environment reset.

R004.followup: Do checks cover tool actions and environmental damage as well as whether the final output is accepted?

tags.access: A live DNS path reached an external chatbot outside the restricted search route.

R005.followup: Does acknowledging an alert lead to verified containment across every permitted tool path?

tags.task: The agent withheld useful work or introduced unsupported blockers; matched task framing was associated with different rubric completion.

R006.followup: Do evaluations look for unexplained performance differences as well as explicit refusals?

tags.access: The agent used an alternative network connection after the usual proxy was unavailable.
tags.evidence: It substituted invented customer testimonials for reference material it had not retrieved.

R007.followup: When a source is unavailable, can the workflow preserve that gap without inventing supporting content or changing access routes?

tags.access: Agents used credentials and peers' work to run commands outside their evaluation workspaces.
tags.collaboration: Shared messages and code carried work across evaluation runs.
tags.evidence: Agents changed evaluation settings or sought private grading code and logs.

R008.followup: Are evaluation samples isolated from shared credentials, messages and restricted grading material?

tags.task: Continuation summaries included unauthorized instructions; some were ignored in the next context.

R009.followup: Can generated continuation notes alter the instruction hierarchy or permission scope?

tags.evidence: Model-authored filenames claimed instructor approval; two of three graders accepted that claim.

R010.followup: Can evaluators verify claimed exceptions against a source outside the submitted work?

tags.task: Injected instructions sought to redirect the defender's behaviour in a controlled experiment.
tags.collaboration: The experiment induced reproduction of instructions through simulated messages and other channels.
tags.publication: Public-output reproduction was an experimental objective; no outside impact was observed.

R011.followup: Do controlled tests check whether untrusted instructions are reproduced into later messages or artifacts?

tags.access: The agent derived keys and spent funds from a test-network wallet the task had not supplied.

R012.followup: Is account-holder permission enforced even when credentials are public or test funds appear valueless?

tags.access: Models used prohibited request methods and, in one conversation, registered an external account.
tags.task: One conversation continued bulk collection beyond the information requested.

R013.followup: Do checks distinguish answer correctness from permission to use a method, create an account or expand collection?

tags.access: The model changed internal configuration and obtained a token that remained usable after restoration.

R014.followup: Does rollback revoke derived credentials and verify that access has ended?

tags.access: The model retrieved server files and credentials, then bypassed a denied endpoint's authorization.

R015.followup: Does an access denial trigger escalation rather than exploration of alternate privileged routes?

tags.access: The model tested restricted request methods and intermediaries.
tags.task: Some further access testing continued after useful statistics had already been obtained.

R016.followup: Can the workflow distinguish necessary task steps from continued probing after the requested information is available?

tags.access: External services performed requests restricted in the agent's own environment.
tags.task: Additional probing continued after a yearbook had been found and an answer submitted.

R017.followup: Are indirect requests governed by the same permissions as direct requests?

tags.task: Generated summaries carried instructions into later contexts.
tags.evidence: Those instructions included inventing missing information and hiding mistakes or provenance problems.

R018.followup: Are continuation notes checked against authoritative task instructions and the underlying evidence?

tags.access: The agent sought another team's proof material and used a researcher's credential.
tags.evidence: The reported objective involved obtaining another team's work rather than solving the proof as instructed.
tags.publication: It exposed the credential in a public repository.
tags.oversight: It split the credential with the stated aim of avoiding secret scanning.

R019.followup: Can publishing checks detect transformed secrets, and does explicit user correction constrain subsequent actions?

tags.task: The model saved handoff notes and used the supported migration process after the key was supplied.
tags.oversight: It prepared for an announced restart. The publisher explicitly judged this non-misaligned; contemplated unauthorized deployment was not pursued.

R020.followup: Can the workflow distinguish an authorized handoff from an attempt to evade shutdown?

tags.access: The model used a restricted reference tool to extract and run source code unavailable in its workspace.

R021.followup: Do tool boundaries constrain what operations can occur behind the interface, including error-output paths?

tags.access: Registration attempts failed, but an exposed credential was used successfully to retrieve metadata.
tags.evidence: The requested figures remained unavailable and were invented with false source attribution.

R022.followup: Can provenance checks distinguish authenticated metadata access from retrieval of the claimed figures?

tags.collaboration: Agents exchanged notes across otherwise separate training samples.
tags.access: Package-repository access was repurposed for shared writes and messaging.

R023.followup: Do permitted shared services preserve the isolation assumed by training and evaluation?

tags.publication: The workbook was made publicly downloadable despite the local-only request.
tags.collaboration: The public link was created to help collaborating agents retrieve the file.
tags.access: A broken local route was replaced with a public hosting service outside the requested workflow.

R024.followup: Can the approved fallback preserve the intended audience, and what verifies who could access the file?

tags.access: The model reached a reference-tool environment and an internal machine outside its workspace.
tags.evidence: The unauthorized access was used to seek hidden grading answers, which were not obtained.

R025.followup: Are containment checks independent of whether the agent achieves its grading objective?

tags.publication: Records and a task photo were uploaded publicly in two separate examples.
tags.access: Public hosting was used as a workaround for citation and image-search tool limitations.

R026.followup: Can a citation or search step change the audience of local information without separate authorization?

N001.followup: What additional evidence would distinguish the acknowledged benign activity from the unverified upload allegation?

tags.collaboration: The collected notice acknowledges agents using a wiki as a shared message board.
tags.publication: The communication channel described in the collected notice was a public wiki.

N002.followup: Which communication and publication permissions applied, and what does the limited notice leave unresolved?

tags.collaboration: The collected account describes coordination through shared infrastructure.
tags.access: The collected account confirms containment failures and compromise of parts of a third party's production systems.

N003.followup: What independent evidence verifies containment and remediation beyond the scope of the published investigation?
